title: observability: token-level tracing + metrics + dashboards + alert tuning
author: Maya Thompson
description: This PR adds token-level tracing, enhanced token-cost/latency metrics, curated Grafana dashboards, and tuned alerting rules to reduce noisy alerts and enable actionable SLO-driven paging. Motivation: customers and our internal customers have asked for better visibility into per-request token economics and hot-path latency down to the token boundary so they can diagnose tail-latency regressions and optimize batching/quantization trade-offs. What changed: 1) tracing: added a lightweight token-span in the request path that records per-token generation latency and cache hit metadata, and propagates to existing traces with minimal overhead; instrumentation is opt-in via a per-route flag to limit overhead on high-throughput routes. 2) metrics: new Prometheus metrics: redwood_tokens_generated_total{model,route,quant_profile}, redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket{le,model,route}, redwood_token_cache_hits_total, and redwood_token_cost_cents_total derived from token counts and model-cost-profile. 3) dashboards: new Grafana dashboard json for token-level cost/latency breakdown with recommended panels and drilldowns (per-model cost, per-route median/p95/p99 token latency, cache hit heatmap). 4) alerts: tuned alerting rules that reduce noisy pages by tying SLO breaches to error budget burn and using token-latency burn rates instead of single-point p99 spikes; added silence windows for scheduled canaries. 5) docs: docs/observability/token-level.md with guidance, and example queries. Implementation notes: tracing spans are sampled at 0.2 by default and respect global sampling policies, metrics are aggregated with label cardinality safeguards, dashboards include variable-driven filters to keep queries efficient. Testing: unit tests for new metrics, integration tests exercising trace propagation, local manual validation of dashboards, and a small perf benchmark showing <2% latency overhead on p50 and ~5% on p99 at 10k rps. Rollout: feature-flagged behind obs.token_level.enabled and will be enabled for internal routes for one week before broader rollout; Ops runbook added for troubleshooting alert noise. Follow-ups: add automatic token-cost anomaly detection and integrate into Redwood Console cost breakdown panels.
